Stack: Vercel (Fluid Compute / Active CPU pricing — charges for active CPU time + provisioned memory + invocations, not wall-clock GB-seconds), a second Vercel `oci` container service (`containers/function/`), Supabase (Postgres + Auth + Storage), Stripe, Resend, Upstash (rate limiting), Apollo, Customer.io, Composio + Anthropic (embedded agent), Datadog RUM. Check: 1. **Runtime choices per route**: grep every `export const runtime = ...` declaration under `app/api/*`. Nodejs runtime functions generally cost more / cold-start differently than edge under Vercel's model — flag any route using `nodejs` that doesn't strictly need it (per CLAUDE.md, Stripe webhook and OCI-adjacent routes need nodejs; others may not). 2. **The `oci` container service** (`containers/function/`) — a running container service has baseline cost even near-idle. Given CLAUDE.md describes it as "a scaffold/proof-of-concept... not yet a product surface" with a minimal `server.mjs` that just answers health checks, assess whether it's worth its ongoing infra cost today, or whether it should be paused/removed until there's an actual workload. 3. **Image handling**: check `next.config.ts` `images.formats`/`remotePatterns` and where `next/image` is used vs raw `` — unoptimized/uncached image transforms cost money per-transform on Vercel. 4. **Bundle size / `optimizePackageImports`**: is the `experimental.optimizePackageImports` list in `next.config.ts` covering all the heavy packages actually used (check `package.json` deps like `motion`, `lucide-react`, `@radix-ui/*`, `mixpanel-browser`, `posthog-js`)? Larger bundles cost more in egress and slow cold starts. 5. **Unbounded/loop-prone external API calls**: check `lib/agent/index.ts` and `scripts/agent.ts` for any risk of unbounded Claude/Composio API call loops (cost risk, not just correctness). Check `lib/apollo.ts`, `lib/customerio.ts` for retry logic that could cause request amplification. 6. **Supabase query efficiency**: check admin list-view queries (`app/admin/leads`, `app/admin/bookings`, `app/admin/users`, `app/admin/projects`) for N+1 patterns or missing `.limit()`/pagination — unbounded reads cost more and get slower as tables grow. Cross-reference against indexes defined in `supabase/migrations/*.sql`. 7. **Third-party script loading** (`app/layout.tsx`, `components/analytics-provider.tsx`) — redundant/overlapping analytics providers (PostHog + Mixpanel + GA4 + GTM + Datadog all firing) is both a perf and a cost-per-event consideration across 4-5 paid analytics platforms. Report back (final message, plain text): ranked findings, each with file:line where relevant, one-sentence description of the cost inefficiency, estimated impact (High/Medium/Low — qualitative, no need for dollar figures), and a one-sentence fix/recommendation. Cap at ~12 most significant.

input.message:
Cost-optimization review of dobeu.net v3 (branch feature/hardening-audit-and-landing-refresh). RESEARCH ONLY — no files changed. Ranked by cost impact.

Note: `next.config.js` no longer exists (only `next.config.ts`), so the CLAUDE.md "duplicate config shadows CSP" warning is now STALE — the .ts config (CSP, images, optimizePackageImports) is the active one. Worth updating CLAUDE.md.

=== HIGH IMPACT ===

1. Supabase session refresh runs on EVERY request via Node middleware — middleware.ts:6,13 (`runtime="nodejs"` + `updateSession()`). Every non-static request (incl. anonymous marketing-page hits, the highest-traffic surface) spins up a Node function invocation AND makes a network round-trip to Supabase Auth to refresh a session that anonymous visitors don't have. Under Vercel Active-CPU pricing this is invocations + active CPU + Supabase Auth load on 100% of page views. Fix: scope the matcher to only auth-bearing surfaces (`/portal`, `/admin`, `/login`, `/auth`) so the public landing skips the Supabase call entirely, or short-circuit updateSession when no `sb-*` auth cookie is present.

2. The `oci` container service is pure standby cost for zero product value — vercel.json:13-39, containers/function/server.mjs. CLAUDE.md itself calls it "a scaffold/proof-of-concept... not yet a product surface"; server.mjs only answers `/`, `/health`, `/healthz` with static JSON. A `runtime:container` service carries provisioned-memory/min-instance baseline cost even at idle. Fix: remove the `oci` service + `/oci` rewrites (and the middleware matcher exclusion) from vercel.json until there's a real workload; keep the source dir. Biggest single line-item win.

3. Admin list queries with no `.limit()` / pagination — app/admin/users/page.tsx:8-11 (`profiles` unbounded), app/admin/projects/page.tsx:9-17 (both `projects` AND `profiles` unbounded), app/admin/invoices/page.tsx:19-20 (`profiles` limit 500, `projects` limit 500 — high but bounded). These full-table reads grow linearly with the tables and run on each admin page load (force-dynamic, service-role, RLS bypassed so no natural row filter). Also app/admin/projects and invoices load the ENTIRE profiles table just to build an owner-name lookup map — an N+1-style over-fetch. Fix: add `.limit()` + pagination, and replace full-profiles-table joins with a targeted `.in("id", ownerIds)` fetch.

=== MEDIUM IMPACT ===

4. `optimizePackageImports` misses several heavy client packages — next.config.ts:136 only lists `lucide-react, motion, @radix-ui/react-dialog, @radix-ui/react-tabs`. Missing from package.json: `posthog-js`, `mixpanel-browser`, `@datadog/browser-rum`+`browser-logs` (both 5.35.1), `date-fns`, `@tanstack/react-table`, and ~12 other `@radix-ui/*` packages (accordion, dropdown-menu, select, popover, etc.). Larger client bundles = more egress + slower hydration. Fix: add the tree-shakeable ones (all @radix-ui/*, date-fns, lucide already there) to the list; note posthog/mixpanel/datadog are lazy-loaded so lower priority.

5. Five overlapping paid analytics platforms all fire on the same events — components/analytics-provider.tsx (GTM + GA4 + Vercel Analytics + SpeedInsights) plus lib/analytics.ts fans out to PostHog + Mixpanel + GA4 + GTM, and Datadog RUM via initDatadog. That's per-event billing across PostHog, Mixpanel, and Datadog simultaneously capturing largely redundant product-analytics data, plus GA4/GTM. Fix: pick one product-analytics tool (PostHog OR Mixpanel, not both — they overlap almost entirely) and drop the other; keep GA4 for marketing attribution. Halves event-ingestion cost on two paid platforms.

6. `motion` (framer-motion successor, v12) is a large dependency — package.json:57. If only used for a handful of landing animations, it's heavy for the payload. Fix: audit actual usage; consider `motion/react` lazy import or CSS transitions for simple cases. (Lower confidence — didn't enumerate all usages.)

=== LOW IMPACT ===

7. Remote image transform hosts configured but founder avatar is already local — next.config.ts:140-148 allows unsplash/licdn/github/blob remote patterns (each remote `next/image` transform is billed per source image on Vercel). The one Hero image (Hero.tsx:313, FOUNDER.avatar) is local `/images/jeremy-williams.jpg` — good, no transform cost. Just confirm the /repos GitHub-avatar images (avatars.githubusercontent.com) are the only remote-transform consumers; those ARE billed per unique avatar. Fix: consider `unoptimized` for GitHub avatars (already tiny) to skip the transform charge.

8. `github-activity` route is well-optimized already — app/api/github-activity/route.ts:14,122,141: `revalidate=300` + `s-maxage=300, stale-while-revalidate=600` + graceful fallback. No action; noting as a good pattern to replicate elsewhere. nodejs runtime here is forced by "Vercel Services does not support Edge outputs" (route comment line 12), so the nodejs choice is a platform constraint, not waste — same applies to all the nodejs routes flagged in the brief.

=== On the runtime=nodejs question (brief item 1) ===
All 11 `app/api/*` routes + apple-icon + middleware use `runtime="nodejs"`, but this is NOT low-hanging fruit here: the codebase comments (github-activity/route.ts:12, middleware.ts:4-5) state Vercel Services rejects Edge Function outputs for this project, so edge isn't available as an option. Stripe webhook genuinely needs nodejs (SDK). So the cost lever is NOT switching to edge — it's reducing HOW OFTEN nodejs functions invoke (finding #1, the middleware matcher) and removing the standby container (#2).

=== On agent loop risk (brief item 5) ===
lib/agent/index.ts and scripts/agent.ts: no unbounded-loop cost risk found. `runAgent()` runs a single `query()` stream and the /api/agent route is admin-gated with `maxDuration=60`. The `for await` over the stream is bounded by the SDK. apollo.ts uses `Promise.any` over 2 endpoint candidates (bounded, no retry amplification); customerio.ts has no retries. All lead-pipeline external calls are single-shot best-effort. No amplification concerns.

Top 3 to action: (1) narrow the middleware matcher so anonymous marketing traffic skips the Supabase session refresh, (2) remove the idle `oci` container service, (3) add limits/pagination to the unbounded admin queries.

Relevant files: C:\Users\JeremyWilliams\repos\new-dobeu-net\middleware.ts, \vercel.json, \next.config.ts, \components\analytics-provider.tsx, \lib\analytics.ts, \app\admin\users\page.tsx, \app\admin\projects\page.tsx, \app\admin\invoices\page.tsx, \containers\function\server.mjs.

These full-table reads grow linearly with the tables and run on each admin page load (force-dynamic, service-role, RLS bypassed so no natural row filter). Also app/admin/projects and invoices load the ENTIRE profiles table just to build an owner-name lookup map — an N+1-style over-fetch. Fix: add `.limit()` + pagination, and replace full-profiles-table joins with a targeted `.in("id", ownerIds)` fetch.

content.text:
Cost-optimization review complete. Report sent to team-lead. Summary of what I found:

**High impact**
1. **Middleware runs Supabase session refresh on every request** (`middleware.ts:6,13`) — including anonymous marketing traffic, the highest-volume surface. Node invocation + Supabase Auth round-trip on 100% of page views. Narrow the matcher to auth-bearing paths.
2. **The `oci` container service is idle standby cost** (`vercel.json:13-39`) — a scaffold that only answers health checks, but `runtime:container` carries baseline cost. Biggest single line-item win to remove until there's a workload.
3. **Unbounded admin list queries** (`app/admin/users`, `projects`, `invoices`) — full-table reads with no `.limit()`, plus loading the entire `profiles` table for owner-name lookups.

**Medium**: `optimizePackageImports` misses ~15 heavy packages; five overlapping paid analytics platforms (PostHog + Mixpanel + Datadog + GA4 + GTM) double-billing on the same events.

**Notable stale-doc finding**: `next.config.js` no longer exists, so CLAUDE.md's "duplicate config shadows CSP" warning is now false — the `.ts` config is active.

**Cleared as non-issues**: no unbounded agent/API loops; the `runtime=nodejs` choices are a Vercel Services platform constraint (edge isn't available), so the cost lever is invocation *frequency*, not runtime switching.
